name: Squirting — The Pattern Recognition Principle
summary: There's no single magic method—techniques vary enormously. The one reliable rule: whatever leads to squirting first causes a weird, unfamiliar feeling (tension, queasiness, or need-to-pee). That feeling is the sign you're on the right path—do more of what caused it.
detailed_description: Because squirting techniques differ so much from person to person, the useful pattern is the precursor sensation, not a specific motion. Every path to squirting tends to start with an odd, unfamiliar feeling inside—tension, queasiness, or a having-to-pee sensation. Many people stop right there because it doesn't match expected pleasure patterns; the key is to recognize it as a green light and continue doing whatever produced it. To find your method, think back to what you were doing when you last felt that unfamiliar sensation—you probably stopped, so try continuing instead.
stepwise_structure: 1. Don't search for one 'correct' technique—methods vary widely (G-region, gentle clitoral, and others).
2. Pay attention to precursor sensations: tension inside, queasiness, or a need-to-pee feeling.
3. Treat that weird feeling as the green light, not a red flag.
4. Keep doing—and do more of—whatever caused it.
5. Recall what you were doing the last time you felt it and resume that instead of stopping.
6. Partner guidance: if they hit that tension sensation, don't immediately stop—continue gently.
safety_notes: The need-to-pee feeling is expected; continuing is safe if it stays comfortable.
Keep communication open—'more of that' should still feel okay, not painful.

meta.core_principle: The weird/unfamiliar feeling (tension, queasiness, need-to-pee) is the signal to continue, not stop.
possible_methods: methods that vary by individual anatomy
